headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: Windsurf’s shared filesystem/clipboard/MCP surfaces can ingest untrusted content, while the paired source-available prompt-leak repo offers no isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, clipboard, and MCP content by default, so it may ingest attacker-controlled text as instructions. The source-available system_prompts_leaks repo is about prompt leakage and provides no isolation or provenance controls. The pair creates a plausible injection bridge, though not a documented direct exploit.
conditions: IF content from workspace files, clipboard, or an MCP server is treated as instructions by Windsurf
IF the system_prompts_leaks repo is copied into a workspace that Windsurf reads
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based prompt ingestion for the session
Keep untrusted files in a separate workspace
Require manual review before MCP tool calls
Use a read-only clone of the repo
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and MCP inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and can send content to its model proxy or MCP servers, so sensitive source code or open files can leave the local workspace. The paired repo is source-available and unverified, so if it contains leaked prompts or secrets, Windsurf may ingest them and transmit them onward. The interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or open files are present in the Windsurf workspace
IF Windsurf forwards file contents to its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before opening it
Disable MCP servers for the session
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace
Rotate any exposed keys after review
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before model upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress, and its concurrency model shares state via the local filesystem. The paired repo is source-available and may be edited or cloned into the same workspace, creating overlapping writes and git-state races. Because no locking is documented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF two Windsurf instances or another editor touch the same local workspace
IF git state is modified concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits in the same workspace
Use one agent per repository clone
Commit or stash before switching agents
Turn off auto-execute for terminal commands
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on file and MCP outputs, so if it consumes content from the system_prompts_leaks repo as authoritative, downstream edits or commands may follow bad instructions. The repo itself is about leaked prompts and is not a verified source of truth. This is a plausible default workflow risk, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses repository text as authoritative guidance without verification
IF terminal auto-execute is enabled for commands derived from that text
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated commands
Disable auto-execute
Cross-check outputs against trusted docs
Mark the repo as untrusted input
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Windsurf handles source code and open files and may transmit them to a third-party model proxy or MCP servers, which can create policy or residency issues. The paired repo is source-available and does not itself establish a residency mismatch, so only Windsurf is directly implicated. The compliance risk is present but narrower than medium.
conditions: IF regulated source code, secrets, or customer data are opened in Windsurf
IF the configured model proxy or MCP server is outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Open only non-regulated files
Disable external MCP servers
Confirm the model endpoint jurisdiction
Remove secrets before editing
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
